newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia loans and advances up 2.3 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia loans and advances up 2.3 pct in July.

text.p: The Malaysian central bank said on Monday that total loans and advances extended to banking institutions in July rose 2.3 percent year-on-year against June's 1.2 percent growth.

Excluding housing loans sold to national mortgage corporation, July's total loans and advances was up by 6.4 billion ringgit, Bank Negara said in a statement on Malaysian monetary and banking developements in July.

The increase in loans was chanelled mainly to finance, insurance and business services (2.4 billion ringgit), broad property (782 million ringgit), as well as for consumption purposes (1.2 billion), the statement said.
"Nevertheless, the annual growth of total loans continued to moderate to 27.4 percent at the end of July, from 28.8 percent at the end of the previous month," Bank Negara said.
The banking system experienced a small resource gap in July as loans outpaced deposits, the central bank said.
The gap of 236 million ringgit compared with a 493 million surplus in June and a one billion ringgit gap in May.
